notes: Libretto by Lorenzo Da Ponte (1786). Words follow the engraving's spelling (quì beside qui, ajutarvi/ajutarti, jer, ruina, veggio, un' insidia, all' impostor, dell' uso, ch'ho beside che ho, e for è in 'e sicuro il vostro onor', Dei with a capital, 'Pian, pian in su' printed as three words where the libretto has 'pian pianin su'). IPA follows sung Italian conventions: stressed syllable marked, elisions (two words on one note in the score) joined with ‿, open e/o as ɛ/ɔ, intervocalic s voiced (cosa, muso, uso, paurosa, sorpreso, rinchiuso, tesor), così with [s], nasal assimilation across and within words (im ˈmal, soŋ ˈkwi, ˈpjam pjaˈni.no, riŋˈkju.zo); ruina is sung in three syllables (ru.i.na); mai, Dei, mio, io, trovai and the pau of paurosa each fall on one note but are written with both vowels (ˈma.i, ˈdɛ.i). Translation literal, for meaning.
